evidence: Posted "QA Automation Engineer" job with title, industry Technology, type Full-time, location Remote, salary 90000-120000, description, skills Playwright/Selenium. Job appeared in employer dashboard (Active Jobs 6→ includes new job) and in job-seeker listing (Showing 9 jobs, new card visible with all fields).

Submitted application (name, email, phone, message) on job detail page; toast "Application submitted! Your application for QA Automation Engineer at TechCorp Solutions has been sent." appeared and form cleared.

After submission, toast confirmation shown; dashboard shows job-1787670353332 Applications(1) with exactly one record: Jane Tester / jane.tester@example.com / 555-0199 / message matching submitted data.
Clicking the applications toggle (count button) on a dashboard job expanded an Applications list showing the submitted application details.
Dashboard "Active Jobs"=6 matches 6 listed jobs; "Total Applications"=4 matches sum of per-job counts (1+2+1+0+0+0=4).

Job detail page for new listing shows title, company (TechCorp Solutions), industry, employment type, location, salary range, posted date, full description text, and required skills (Playwright, Selenium) matching what was submitted.
Dashboard application record for Jane Tester displays name, email, phone (555-0199), message, and a submission date ("Yesterday") as a distinct record item.

issue: Incorrect relative date display for newly created records
actual: Job posted at current session time (current date 2026-08-25) shows "Posted Yesterday" on both job card and job detail page instead of "Today"/"just now". The application submitted moments later also shows submission date as "Yesterday" in the employer dashboard instead of today's date. This indicates a date/timezone off-by-one bug.

issue: No persistence of app state across reload
actual: After publishing job "QA Automation Engineer" and submitting an application to it, reloading the page (navigating to http://localhost:6003/) caused the job listing count to revert from 9 to 8 and the new job disappeared entirely from the job-seeker listing; the submitted application was lost as well. Data is stored only in-memory client-side and is not persisted (no backend/localStorage), so published jobs and applications do not survive a reload.

evidence: All 8 job cards on home page display title, company, industry badge, employment type badge, location, salary range, posting date, and skill tags (e.g. job-1: Senior Frontend Developer, TechCorp Solutions, Technology, Full-time, San Francisco CA, $140k-$180k, Jan 15, React/TypeScript/CSS/Node.js).
Home page shows "Showing 8 jobs" matching the 8 rendered job cards; clicking a card (job-3 Registered Nurse) navigated to /jobs/job-3 and displayed its details.
Industry=Technology alone → 2 jobs (job-1,job-7). Adding Location=Seattle,WA combined → 1 job (job-7). Clear filters restored 8 jobs. Employment Type=Part-time alone → 1 job (job-6, Part-time).

Search "FIGMA" (uppercase) matched job-2 by skill "Figma". Search "techcorp" (lowercase) matched 2 jobs by company "TechCorp Solutions". Search "nurse" matched job-3 by title "Registered Nurse". Results and count updated immediately with each keystroke.

Each filter/search change immediately updated "Showing N jobs" and the card list. A no-match search ("zzzznonexistentquery") produced "Showing 0 jobs" and a "No jobs found" empty-state message. Clicking Clear filters restored all 8 jobs and reset search/selects to defaults.

Submitting with all fields empty triggered native required-field validation ("Please fill out this field.") and focused the Full Name field; no submission occurred. Submitting with a syntactically invalid email ("not-an-email") triggered native email format validation ("Please include an '@' in the email address...") and focused the Email field; no success toast appeared, form values were retained, and no application was created.

actual: Submitted two separate applications to job-1 (Senior Frontend Developer) using the identical email "dupcheck@test.com" with different names/messages. Both submissions succeeded with a success toast each time, and the employer dashboard shows job-1's application count increased from 2 to 4 (both duplicate-email applications were saved as separate records). No error or rejection was shown for the second, duplicate-email submission.

Submitted a job posting with all required fields filled (title, industry, type, location, description, 1 skill) but Minimum Salary=100000 and Maximum Salary=50000 (min > max). The form accepted it without any error message, showed "Job posted successfully!" toast, and the job now appears in the dashboard/listings displaying an illogical salary range "$100k - $50k". Missing-field validation (native required-field checks) does work correctly, but the min<=max salary constraint is not enforced at all.

evidence: Clicking delete on "Invalid Salary Job" opened an alertdialog "Delete this job?" with Cancel/Delete buttons and warning text about permanent removal of the job and its applications. Confirming Delete removed the job from the employer dashboard (Active Jobs 6→5) and from the job-seeker listing (job no longer present, list back to original 8 jobs).

issue: No edit functionality for published jobs
actual: Inspected the employer dashboard's job listing rows (DOM query for all dashboard.jobs.item.* elements): each job row exposes only two controls — an "applications" toggle button and a "delete" button. There is no edit/pencil button, no clickable link to an edit form, and no aria-label/title indicating an edit action anywhere on the dashboard. The Post a Job form only supports creating new listings (submits via action "post-job"); there is no equivalent edit form or route reachable from the UI. Employers therefore have no way to modify a published job's details.
